title: Match-engine worker OOM runbook for nested RailClear files
subtitle: Diagnose and recover when a 90MB XML-in-JSON payload pins one Kafka partition and kills a pod
author: Aman Kumar
audience: On-call SE II, SRE, and Clearhaven ops during month-end file bursts
owners: Aman Kumar (match-engine), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Priya Nair (EM)
summary: This runbook covers match-engine OutOfMemory kills when a nested RailClear file (XML wrapped in JSON, often 80-96MB, worst case 90.4MB observed on 2024-04-30) lands on a single Kafka partition and one worker tries to batch-deserialize the whole tree. Use it when pods flap, kubectl top shows one replica near the 1.5Gi limit, or Helen Cho pages because RailClear allocations stop matching. It tells you how to confirm the failure, take a heap dump without leaking financial identifiers, split records versus raise memory, and when bumping the limit again is the wrong move.
form_description: Internal on-call runbook for match-engine OOM on nested RailClear payloads. Written after CLH-INC-2024-091 so SE II and SRE share one set of commands and a hard rule against unbounded memory bumps.
revision_history: First draft after INC-2024-091 (90.4MB nested file, partition 7).
Added heap-dump PVC path and PHI/financial handling notes.
Approved. Memory request/limit history and the do-not-bump-again section.

blocks.text: Match-engine worker OOM runbook

Match-engine is the JVM service that consumes RailClear and street-side legs from Kafka topic clh.railclear.inbound.v2, deserializes each record, and writes candidate matches into recon.leg_match_work. The consumer still batches. That was a 2022 decision when files were 4-12MB and nested depth stopped at two levels. Clearhaven's RailClear vendor started emitting nested lot allocations inside a single XML document stuffed into a JSON envelope. One file on 2024-04-30 was 90.4MB on the wire and expanded to roughly 1.84Gi of live objects on the heap because Jackson plus the XML mapper keep both the DOM and the typed allocation list. One partition, one pod, one batch. The pod died. That is this runbook.

I wrote this after CLH-INC-2024-091, which Priya Nair classified as Sev-2 because Helen Cho's ops queue showed 14,611 unmatched RailClear allocations for trade date 2024-04-29 and the 7:20 ET SLA window was already 41 minutes in. Diego Alvarez pulled kubectl top while I was still SSH-ing into the wrong bastion. We recovered by isolating partition 7 and splitting the file offline. We also learned that the 1.5Gi limit we set in January is enough for the 95th percentile file and not enough for the nested shape. Do not treat this as a license to set the limit to 4Gi and walk away.
Decision (read this first)

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: For a nested RailClear OOM, split the file into per-lot Kafka records before you raise memory. The current limit is 1.5Gi request / 1.5Gi limit. Peak heap on the 90.4MB file was 1.97Gi for 11.4 seconds, then the kernel OOM-killed the container. A 2Gi spike on a 1.5Gi cap is expected for this shape. Raising to 2.5Gi hides the next 140MB file. Split is the fix. Memory is a cushion for the split job and for the 99th percentile of files that remain nested for one more release.

Rahul Deshmukh asked in the 2024-05-07 recon standup whether we could just give match-engine 4Gi like the overnight Spark jobs and stop paging. Priya said no, and I agree. Match-engine sits on the ns-eks-clh-prod-01 on-demand node group clh-match-r6i.xlarge (4 vCPU, 30.7Gi allocatable after kube and Datadog). Twelve replicas at 4Gi would pin 48Gi for a service whose p95 RSS is 612Mi. We would starve break-svc and recon-query on the same nodes during month-end. Kavya Menon measured the node pressure on 2024-04-30: when match-engine replica match-engine-7f2c-xk9p sat at 1.48Gi, the node's memory.available dropped to 1.12Gi and kubelet started evicting the log-sidecar on recon-query-6. That is the wrong trade.

blocks.text: When this runbook applies

Use these steps when match-engine is dying and the payload looks like RailClear nested XML, not when the JVM is leaking over hours or when Kafka itself is out of disk. The leak path is a different ticket (CLH-4188, Kavya's weak-hashmap in the match-key cache). The disk path is CLH-RB-2023-012. This runbook is the sudden death of one replica, usually on one partition, usually after a RailClear drop at 18:40 ET or a late restatement at 06:10 ET.

items: Alert MatchEnginePodOOMKilled fires, or kubectl get pod shows Last State OOMKilled with Exit Code 137 on a match-engine replica.
lag on clh.railclear.inbound.v2 grows on a single partition (often 4, 7, or 11 because RailClear keys by account_hash % 16 and a few correspondent books hash together).
Helen Cho or Marcus Bell report that allocations for one correspondent (recently CORR-RLC-4401 and CORR-RLC-2219) stopped matching while other books look fine.
Datadog metric jvm.heap_memory on match-engine jumps from ~480Mi to >1.4Gi in under 20 seconds, then the series goes missing because the pod died.
A file named like 20240429_RAILCLEAR_ALLOC_NESTED_4401.xml.json is sitting in s3://ns-clh-inbound-prod/railclear/landing/ with ContentLength between 78MB and 96MB.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Heap dumps from match-engine contain account numbers, CUSIPs, allocation quantities, and sometimes SSN-shaped tax ids that Clearhaven stuffed into the XML <partyTaxId> node. Do not copy a dump to a laptop. Do not attach it to Jira. Do not paste MAT strings into Slack. Use the forensic PVC and the redaction job in section 6.
Background: why a 90MB file becomes a 2Gi spike

RailClear files arrive as a JSON object with keys fileId, receivedAt, and xmlBase64. The consumer decodes the base64, runs it through com.northstar.clearhaven.railclear.XmlAllocationMapper, and builds a List<NestedLot>. The mapper is DOM-based. We kept DOM because the schema has recursive <lot> under <lot> under <block> and StAX kept losing the parent account on depth 5 (Sneha Iyer logged that in CLH-QA-2023-044). DOM means the whole document is a tree of Node objects plus our typed copies. For a flat file of 12,400 allocations the heap delta is about 180Mi. For a nested file of 12,400 allocations with average depth 6.3, the heap delta on 2024-04-30 was 1.51Gi above baseline. Add the Kafka consumer's fetch buffer (fetch.max.bytes is 52,428,800), the JSON envelope, and a full GC that did not finish, and you get the 1.97Gi peak Diego captured from cgroup memory.usage_in_bytes.

Batching makes it worse. match-engine uses a Spring Kafka listener with batch = true and max.poll.records = 80. That value was set when records were 40-90KB. A nested RailClear file is one Kafka record. max.poll.records does not save you. The listener still hands the worker a List of size 1 containing a 90MB string. The batch assembler then copies that string into a ByteArrayOutputStream because the XML mapper API takes a byte[]. Two copies of 90MB plus DOM plus typed list. I timed a local replay on 2024-05-03: 90.4MB file, JVM -Xmx1536m, died at 8.7 seconds into unmarshal. With -Xmx2048m it survived, peaked at 1941Mi, finished in 14.2 seconds. That is the 2Gi spike. The cluster limit is 1.5Gi. Math is not on our side if we leave the file whole.

Historically the Helm chart shipped memory at 512Mi request and 512Mi limit. That was copied from the 2022 proof of concept when we processed CSV. It was too small the first month we took RailClear live (February 2023, CLH-INC-2023-033). We raised to 768Mi in March 2023, 1Gi in August 2023 after the first nested restatement, and 1.5Gi on 2024-01-18 after CLH-MEM-2023-027 (the k8s compute memo). 1.5Gi covers p99 of files from January through March 2024 (p99 size 31.6MB, p99 heap 1.12Gi). It does not cover the nested shape that RailClear started sending for correspondent 4401 in April. Marcus Bell confirmed with the vendor that nested lots are now the default for any block with more than 40 child allocations. That is a standing change. We will see this file shape every month-end until the splitter is in the ingest path, which Kavya has on CLH-4502 with a target of 2024-07-12.

rows: Raised to 768Mi, still died on 22MB restatements
Survived flat files, nested still unknown
Raised after the incident, not before

blocks.text: Preconditions

You need prod-read on ns-eks-clh-prod-01 and prod-write if you are going to cordon a replica or patch a limit. Diego's on-call rotation holds cluster-admin. SE II holds namespace admin for clearhaven-prod except for ResourceQuota changes. If you need to raise memory, you need Priya's Slack OK in #clh-prod-changes and a Helm PR against values-prod.yaml. If you need to touch Postgres while draining, stop. This failure is not a database failure. Rina Das will be unhappy if you take an access exclusive lock on recon.leg_match_work at 19:10 ET because you panicked.

items: Confirm you are in the right cluster: kubectl config current-context should be ns-eks-clh-prod-01. The staging cluster is ns-eks-clh-stg-01 and has a 512Mi limit on purpose so we can reproduce OOM there.
Announce in #clh-oncall: starting CLH-RB-2024-007, suspected nested RailClear OOM, partition if known, file name if known.
Page Diego if the node is also under memory pressure (memory.available < 1.5Gi on the node that hosts the dying replica). Do not page Rina.
If Helen is already on the bridge, ask her for the correspondent id and the RailClear fileId from the vendor portal. FileId maps to the Kafka key.

blocks.text: Confirm it is this failure

The cheap confirmation is kubectl top plus the previous container's last logs. The expensive confirmation is a heap dump. Start cheap. If top shows one replica at 1.4Gi+ and the others at 400-700Mi, you have partition skew plus a fat record, which is this failure. If all replicas climb together, you have a leak or a broadcast storm, and this runbook will waste your time.

# context and namespace
kubectl config current-context
# expect: ns-eks-clh-prod-01

kubectl -n clearhaven-prod get deploy match-engine -o wide
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod get pods -l app=match-engine -o wide

# live memory. If a pod is already dead this is empty for that replica.
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod top pods -l app=match-engine --containers

# why it died
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod get pod -l app=match-engine \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason}{" "}{.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.exitCode}{"\n"}{end}'

# events on the replica you care about
POD=$(kubectl -n clearhaven-prod get pod -l app=match-engine --sort-by=.status.startTime -o jsonpath='{.items[-1:].metadata.name}')
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod describe pod "$POD" | sed -n '/Events:/,$p'

# previous logs; look for RailClear fileId and Jackson / XML mapper
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod logs "$POD" --previous --tail=200 | egrep -i 'OOM|OutOfMemory|RailClear|fileId|NestedLot|XmlAllocationMapper|partition'

# consumer lag by partition (kcat from ops-bastion-03.internal.northstar.example)
kcat -b kafka-clh-prod-01.internal.northstar.example:9092 -C -t clh.railclear.inbound.v2 -f '%p %k %S\n' -o -1 -c 16
# %S is message size in bytes. A 90e6 size on one partition is the smoking gun.

# consumer group lag
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/kafka-tools -- \
  kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-clh-prod-01.internal.northstar.example:9092 \
  --group match-engine-prod --describe
blocks.caption: First-pass diagnosis. Run from ops-bastion-03 or the on-call laptop with the prod kubeconfig. Do not run kcat consume without -c or you will drain the topic in your terminal.

rows: One replica 1400-1512Mi, others normal, or that replica missing
All partitions lagging: broker or DB
file size > 40MB or depth >= 4, then silence
1.0-1.6Gi on the node of the fat replica
all correspondents stuck: match-engine down entirely
blocks.caption: Quick differential. If the table says something else, stop this runbook.

blocks.text: Read the Kafka record size without printing the payload

Printing a 90MB XML blob into Slack or into your scrollback is how financial identifiers leave the building. kcat %S prints size only. If you need the fileId, decode the JSON keys with jq and stop. Do not pretty-print xmlBase64.

# size and key only, last 50 records on a hot partition. Example: partition 7.
kcat -b kafka-clh-prod-01.internal.northstar.example:9092 \
  -C -t clh.railclear.inbound.v2 -p 7 -o -50 -c 50 -f '%p %o %k %S %T\n'

# fileId only, still no XML. Uses a throwaway consumer; do not commit.
kcat -b kafka-clh-prod-01.internal.northstar.example:9092 \
  -C -t clh.railclear.inbound.v2 -p 7 -o -1 -c 1 -J \
  | jq '{key: .key, fileId: .payload.fileId, receivedAt: .payload.receivedAt, xmlChars: (.payload.xmlBase64 | length)}'
blocks.caption: Safe inspection. xmlChars around 1.21e8 corresponds to a ~90MB base64 payload. That is the nested file.

blocks.text: Immediate mitigation

Goal: stop the crash loop, drain the other partitions, keep Helen's queue moving for every correspondent except the one stuck in the fat file. You will isolate the hot partition by shrinking the consumer to a debug pod that does not subscribe, or by publishing a skip marker. The standing method after INC-2024-091 is pause the consumer group on that partition, split the file, republish lots as individual records, then resume. Do not delete the Kafka record. Audit needs it.

items: Identify the hot partition from kafka-consumer-groups --describe. Note CURRENT-OFFSET, LOG-END-OFFSET, LAG, and the member host. The dying pod's broker assignment is in the member ID.
Scale match-engine from 12 to 11 only if the dying replica is crash-looping so hard that kubelet is burning CPU. Prefer leaving replica count alone and pausing the partition.
Pause the partition with the consumer group tool. This is the command Diego and I used on 2024-04-30 at 19:26 ET.
Tell Helen which correspondent is paused. She will manually hold those breaks. Give her the fileId.
Copy the source file from S3 landing to the splitter working bucket. Do not pull it to your laptop.

Run the splitter (next section). Verify lot count against the vendor control total Helen reads from the RailClear portal. On 2024-04-30 the control total was 18,447 lots and we emitted 18,447 records. If you are short, do not resume.
Publish split records to clh.railclear.inbound.v2 with the same key prefix plus /lot/{lotId} so they hash across partitions. Keep railclear_file_id on every record.
Resume the paused partition. Watch top and lag for 10 minutes. Peak RSS should stay under 800Mi.

blocks.text:
# pause one partition for group match-engine-prod (needs kafka-acl: Alter on group)
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/kafka-tools -- \
  kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-clh-prod-01.internal.northstar.example:9092 \
  --group match-engine-prod --topic clh.railclear.inbound.v2 --partitions 7 --reset-offsets --to-current --execute
# then use the pause script we keep in the tools image:
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/kafka-tools -- \
  /opt/ns/pause-partitions.sh --group match-engine-prod --topic clh.railclear.inbound.v2 --partitions 7

# copy landing file to splitter prefix (from ops-bastion-03, role ns-clh-inbound-rw)
aws s3 cp s3://ns-clh-inbound-prod/railclear/landing/20240429_RAILCLEAR_ALLOC_NESTED_4401.xml.json \
  s3://ns-clh-inbound-prod/railclear/split-work/20240429_RAILCLEAR_ALLOC_NESTED_4401.xml.json

# splitter job (image 1.4.2, the one Kavya tagged after the depth-6 fix)
kubectl -n clearhaven-batch delete job railclear-split-manual --ignore-not-found
kubectl -n clearhaven-batch apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: railclear-split-manual
  namespace: clearhaven-batch
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: railclear-splitter
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: split
        image: 111111111111.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ns-clh/railclear-splitter:1.4.2
        args:
        - --src=s3://ns-clh-inbound-prod/railclear/split-work/20240429_RAILCLEAR_ALLOC_NESTED_4401.xml.json
        - --dst-topic=clh.railclear.inbound.v2
        - --mode=per-lot
        - --preserve-file-id=true
        - --max-record-bytes=1048576
        env:
        - name: BOOTSTRAP
          value: kafka-clh-prod-01.internal.northstar.example:9092
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: "1", memory: "3Gi" }
          limits: { cpu: "2", memory: "3Gi" }
EOF

# watch lot count vs control total
kubectl -n clearhaven-batch logs -f job/railclear-split-manual | egrep 'lots_emitted|control_total|ERROR'

# resume
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec deploy/kafka-tools -- \
  /opt/ns/resume-partitions.sh --group match-engine-prod --topic clh.railclear.inbound.v2 --partitions 7

# confirm we are not dying again
watch -n 5 'kubectl -n clearhaven-prod top pods -l app=match-engine --containers'
blocks.caption: Pause, split, resume. Replace partition 7 and the file name with the incident values. Splitter memory is 3Gi on purpose; it is a Job, not the online fleet.

blocks.text: Heap dump, carefully

Take a dump only if split is blocked (splitter image missing, S3 object gone, or you cannot prove the record is nested XML) and you need evidence for Priya or for the vendor. A dump of match-engine on this workload is about 1.1-1.6Gi on disk and contains the full DOM. That is account-level financial data. Clearhaven's Marcus Bell has already told us that a dump leaving Northstar systems is a reportable event for them. Treat it like PHI even though this is a broker-dealer: same handling, same PVC, same 72-hour delete.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Do not use kubectl cp of /tmp/heap.hprof to your laptop. Do not jmap from a personal JumpHost. Do not open the dump in VisualVM on a cafe Wi-Fi. The only approved path is jcmd on the pod, write to /heap-forensics (PVC ns-clh-heap-forensics, encrypted, no public endpoint), then run the redaction Job which zeros xml text nodes and tax id fields before any human downloads a 40MB summary.

# pick a live replica that is climbing but not yet dead. If it is already OOMKilled, dump is gone.
POD=$(kubectl -n clearhaven-prod get pod -l app=match-engine -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')

# confirm the PVC is mounted. Chart 1.19+ mounts it at /heap-forensics.
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec "$POD" -- ls -ld /heap-forensics

# dump. jcmd is in the distroless debug variant; chart 1.19.4+ uses eclipse-temurin with jcmd.
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec "$POD" -- jcmd 1 GC.heap_dump /heap-forensics/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$POD.hprof

# if jcmd is missing, this is the fallback. It still writes to the PVC.
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod exec "$POD" -- \
  sh -c 'jmap -dump:format=b,file=/heap-forensics/'"$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"'-'"$POD"'.hprof 1'

# kick redaction. Output is a histogram plus class names, no XML text.
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod apply -f /opt/ns/runbooks/heap-redact-job.yaml
# then
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod logs -f job/heap-redact | tail

# download ONLY the redacted summary (usually 28-45MB) to the forensics bucket, not to a laptop
aws s3 cp s3://ns-clh-forensics-prod/heap-redacted/$(date -u +%Y%m%d)/summary.txt \
  s3://ns-clh-forensics-prod/heap-redacted/inbox-aman/
blocks.caption: Heap dump path. If jcmd fails because the container is distroless, use the debug copy annotation in the chart rather than docker cp.

blocks.text: What you are looking for in the redacted summary: retained size of com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.dom.DeferredElementImpl, our NestedLot[], and byte[] copies of the JSON envelope. On the 2024-04-30 dump (taken on staging replay, not prod, because prod died too fast) DeferredElementImpl held 612Mi, NestedLot[] 188Mi, byte[] 271Mi. That distribution means DOM, not a leak in match-key Redis. If you instead see com.northstar.clearhaven.match.MatchKeyCache over 400Mi, you are on CLH-4188 and this runbook's split will not help.
Increase memory versus split records

Split records means the ingest path emits one Kafka record per lot, with nested parents flattened into columns parent_block_id, parent_account, depth, and the original xml fragment stored in S3 not in the record. Match-engine then deserializes a 4-40KB JSON object. Heap delta per record stays around 1.2-3.8MB. Batching 80 of those is 100-300MB, which fits in 1.5Gi with room for GC. The splitter is slower at ingest (we measured 18,447 lots in 6.4 minutes on the 3Gi Job) and you lose the ability to reject the whole file as a unit. Helen cares about that last point. The control total check has to happen in the splitter, not in match-engine.

Increasing memory means patching resources.limits.memory on the Deployment or, correctly, a Helm PR. A one-replica patch of 2Gi will often let a 90MB file complete. I did this on staging. It completed, wrote 18,447 rows, and the next nested file at 118MB (synthetic, made from two concatenated vendor samples) died at 2Gi as well. So 2Gi is not a ceiling, it is a delay. The dangerous spike is already 1.97Gi on a 90.4MB file. Linear-ish with DOM size. A 140MB nested file, which Marcus says the vendor has produced in their UAT for a different customer, would want about 3.1Gi. We are not going to size the online fleet for a file we can split in 6 minutes.

blocks.caption: Sizing evidence. Estimates marked. Prod observation is the 90.4MB row.

blocks.text: When you may bump memory anyway

Helen and Marcus get a vote when settlement risk is real. If the splitter Job cannot start (ECR outage, batch namespace quota, S3 403) and the 7:20 ET window is inside 25 minutes, Priya can approve a time-boxed bump. The bump is one replica, 2Gi limit, annotated with expire-by. Diego reverts it before the next business day open. You open CLH-xxxx titled revert match-engine memory bump, assigned to me or to whoever is on call. This is an exception, not a third option in the decision table.

# time-boxed one-replica bump. Prefer Helm. This patch is the emergency form.
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod patch deploy match-engine --type='json' -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"2Gi"},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"2Gi"}
]'

# this rolls ALL replicas. If you truly need one replica only, use a debug Deployment match-engine-fat
# with a unique consumer group, which we rejected in INC-2024-091 because offsets diverge. Do not do that.

# set a reminder annotation
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod annotate deploy match-engine \
  northstar.example/memory-bump-expiry='2024-05-01T12:00:00Z' --overwrite

# revert the next morning, do not forget
kubectl -n clearhaven-prod apply -f <(helm template match-engine chart/ -f values-prod.yaml)
blocks.caption: Emergency memory bump. Rolls the fleet. Tell Diego before you patch so he can watch node allocatable.

blocks.text: When NOT to just bump memory again

This section exists because three people (Rahul in standup, a well-meaning contractor on the Jan compute memo thread, and me at 19:40 on April 30) reached for the Helm values first. Bumping is the move that feels like progress while the DOM is still in the heap. Here is when you will not do it.

items: The file is larger than 40MB and nested depth is >= 4. Split. A bump trains the vendor that we will swallow unbounded trees.
You already bumped once this quarter. January put us at 1.5Gi. April is not January. The standing limit does not crawl up every incident.
Node allocatable on clh-match-r6i.xlarge would drop below 2.4Gi free after the bump. Diego's eviction threshold is 1.5Gi free. We already evicted a sidecar on April 30 at 1.5Gi match-engine RSS.
The record is malformed XML, not large XML. Bumping will still die or will write garbage lots. DLQ it. Ticket the vendor through Marcus.
Only one partition is hot and the key is a single correspondent. That is skew. Splitting lots also spreads keys. A memory bump leaves the skew in place for the next file.
You cannot say when you will revert. An expiry date in an annotation is mandatory. If you will not set one, you will not patch.
Staging has not reproduced it. If you cannot kill a pod on ns-eks-clh-stg-01 with the same file, you do not understand the failure and a prod memory bump is gambling.

The spike is 2Gi and you are about to ask for 4Gi for the whole fleet. That request died in CLH-MEM-2023-027 and it dies here. Cost is about $1,140/month extra on the match node group at 12 replicas, and it still loses to a 140MB file.

blocks.text: If the fix is always more heap, we do not have a match-engine, we have a file parser we deployed twelve times. Split the record.
blocks.attrib: Priya Nair, 2024-05-07 standup, paraphrased with her OK

blocks.text: Rejected alternatives

Disable nested parsing and treat xmlBase64 as an opaque blob stored on S3, with match-engine reading only a vendor-supplied flat sidecar CSV. Kavya floated this on 2024-05-02 because it would make the JVM payload 80KB again. It died the same afternoon. Helen Cho needs nested lot-to-block quantities to explain allocation breaks to Clearhaven middle office. The sidecar CSV the vendor offered (we saw a sample) drops parent_block_id on 11.6% of rows and has no depth field. Marcus asked the vendor for a corrected flat extract; they said 2024 Q4 at earliest. We cannot wait until Q4 while month-end nested files keep arriving.

Run match-engine on a dedicated fat node group with 64Gi RAM and one pod per partition. Diego priced it at $4.7k/month extra for r6i.2xlarge nodes that would sit at 12% CPU on non-month-end days. Priya rejected it on 2024-05-08 as a standing cost to avoid writing a splitter we already have in batch. The splitter Job already requests 3Gi. That is the fat process. It should not be the online fleet.

Drop max.poll.records to 1 and set fetch.max.bytes to 5MB so a 90MB record cannot be fetched. That sounds like protection. It is a poison pill. Kafka will still have a 90MB record, the consumer will retry, and you will stall the partition forever. We tried this on staging. Lag on partition 7 sat at 1 record and never moved. Helen's queue for that correspondent froze with a quieter graph. Worse than OOM because the alert looks like a healthy low-CPU pod.
Failure modes while you are in this runbook

rows: kafka-acl missing Alter on group match-engine-prod
Diego grants a 2-hour ACL. Do not use the super-user bootstrap from the broker pod.
Splitter emits 18,440 lots, control total is 18,447
Do not resume. Re-run with --include-zero-qty. April 30 needed that flag for 7 cancelled lots.

CLH-INC-2024-091's note is the template: fileId, size, partition, lots_emitted, peak RSS, whether you bumped memory, when you reverted. Attach the redacted heap summary if you took a dump. Do not attach the hprof.

Open or update CLH-4502 if the splitter is still not in the automatic ingest path. Until that ships, every nested file is a manual run of this runbook. Appendix: what the JVM flags actually are

People keep asking if we can Xmx our way out. The container has -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 and no explicit -Xmx, on purpose, so a 1.5Gi limit yields about 1.12Gi heap. Direct memory and metaspace sit outside that. The 1.97Gi cgroup peak is heap plus DOM native plus the Kafka client buffer. Raising MaxRAMPercentage to 85 does not get you a 90MB nested file. It gets you a slightly later OOM and a worse GC pause (we saw 4.8s vs 3.1s on staging). Do not patch JVM flags during the incident. Do not add -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError pointing at /tmp; /tmp is emptyDir and dies with the pod, and the dump would still contain the XML. HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError is enabled in staging only, path /heap-forensics, as of chart 1.19.4. Prod will get the same in 1.20 after Diego finishes the PVC backup policy with Rina. Until then, dumps in prod are manual and rare.

If you are tempted to switch the XML mapper to StAX during an incident, stop. The last StAX attempt lost parent_account on depth 5 and Helen spent two days reconciling 2,184 lots by hand (CLH-QA-2023-044). Mapper changes go through Sneha's fixture suite and a staging month-end replay. This runbook does not change parsers. It splits files and, only with Priya's OK, rents 512Mi more RAM until morning.
